headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure; compliance risk is medium.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write configured working directories and uses stdin/stdout plus tool calls; RD-Agent reads files and writes logs, so a shared workspace could let attacker-controlled content from one agent steer the other. No direct shared-channel evidence is provided, so this is inferred from documented surfaces and should be treated conservatively.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b are configured to share the same working directory, prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF either agent parses files from the shared workspace as instructions, attacker-controlled content can influence the other agent.
mitigations: Use separate per-agent directories.
Disable automatic instruction parsing from files.
Add provenance tags to inter-agent handoffs.
Require manual review before copying outputs between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen handles model-provider API keys and can read/write configured files; RD-Agent sends data to external APIs such as OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, DeepSeek, and Kaggle. If they share a workspace, sensitive application data or logs can flow from A into B's outbound requests. The pairwise leakage path is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace, files written by agent_a can be uploaded or summarized by agent_b.
IF sensitive application data is placed in shared logs, agent_b's API calls can transmit it externally.
mitigations: Separate secrets from shared work files.
Redact logs before agent_b reads them.
Restrict agent_b to non-sensitive datasets.
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately if sharing occurred.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen has broad shell, subprocess, filesystem write, and package-install capabilities; RD-Agent has broad network egress and browser access. If both are pointed at the same mutable directory, concurrent writes and external side effects can race or overwrite each other. The profiles do not show locking, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same directory, file clobbering or inconsistent state can occur.
IF either agent mutates shared artifacts without locks, concurrent runs can conflict.
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories.
Serialize writes with a lock file.
Disable concurrent runs on shared artifacts.
Snapshot the workspace before each run.

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen is a multi-agent orchestration framework that can emit tool outputs and code results; RD-Agent is a research automation system that can consume those outputs and act through APIs or browser workflows. If RD-Agent treats AutoGen output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect research actions or reports. No verification step is documented in the profiles.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a outputs without independent validation, incorrect facts can propagate downstream.
IF agent_b uses those outputs to drive API calls or browser actions, the error can affect external work products.
mitigations: Insert a human review gate.
Require schema validation on handoffs.
Cross-check outputs against source data.
Log provenance for every transferred artifact.

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen touches application data and model-provider keys, while RD-Agent touches financial reports, competition datasets, execution traces, and logs and sends data to third-party APIs. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch if regulated or sensitive data is shared across the pair. The profiles do not document aligned compliance controls, so the safer reading is medium.
conditions: IF regulated data such as financial reports or personal data is routed through both agents, compliance obligations may diverge.
IF logs or execution traces are retained by agent_b longer than agent_a's workspace, retention mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared runs.
Set a short log-retention window.
Document data residency for each API call.
Review vendor DPAs before production use.
